issue_request: The Published/Persuasive STU3 issue asked to fix search modifier text that incorrectly said default string search used partial matches at the end of the string; it should say partial matches at the start of the string.
initial_application: Git commit 69d393e31ed270a6e8bcacd1289574fa2209fea3, titled "GF#14390 - fix typo", changed source/search.html from "partial matches at the end of the string" to "partial matches at the start of the string" and records git-svn build@13371, matching the Jira comment.
additional_context: Later search modifier refactors removed the old compact modifier-list wording, but the current source/search.html says default string search matches when a field equals or starts with the supplied value, while :contains matches anywhere within the searched field. The active search modifier code system is consistent, and the 2018 Zulip thread linked from Jira supports :contains as matching anywhere in the string. No conflicting Confluence record was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because current source already preserves the approved correction and no stale source occurrence of the erroneous wording remains.
